The **AvtoVAZ Technical Museum** is a large open-air technology and transport museum in **Tolyatti / Togliatti, Samara Oblast, Russia**, closely associated with **AvtoVAZ**, the maker of Lada cars. It is best known today as the **K. G. Sakharov Park Complex of the History of Technology** or **Technical Museum named after K. G. Sakharov**.

## Basic identity

- **Name:** AvtoVAZ Technical Museum; later commonly known as the **Technical Museum named after K. G. Sakharov**
- **Location:** Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, Russia
- **Founder / origin:** Established with the support of **AvtoVAZ**
- **Opened:** 2001
- **Named after:** **Konstantin Grigoryevich Sakharov**, an AvtoVAZ executive who was one of the key initiators of the museum
- **Type:** Large open-air technical, transport, military, industrial, and automotive museum
- **Main theme:** The history of engineering and technology, especially Soviet and Russian vehicles, military equipment, aviation, rail, and AvtoVAZ/Lada automotive history

## Historical background

The museum was created in the early 2000s as an AvtoVAZ-backed project to preserve examples of Soviet and Russian engineering. Tolyatti is one of Russia’s major industrial cities and is strongly identified with AvtoVAZ, so a technical museum there was a natural extension of the city’s industrial identity.

The project was strongly associated with **K. G. Sakharov**, who supported the idea of collecting and preserving significant machines and vehicles. After his death, the museum was named in his honor.

Over time, the museum expanded beyond AvtoVAZ-related exhibits and became a broad museum of technology, including military hardware, aircraft, railway equipment, agricultural machinery, construction machines, and even a submarine.

## Location and setting

The museum is located in **Tolyatti**, the city built up around the Volga Automobile Plant — AvtoVAZ. Much of the museum is outdoors, with large vehicles displayed across a park-like territory.

Because many of the exhibits are very large — tanks, aircraft, locomotives, ships, and missile systems — the museum is mostly an **open-air exhibition** rather than a traditional indoor museum.

## Size and collection

The collection is large and varied. Different sources give different counts depending on the year and whether restored/storage items are included, but the museum has had **hundreds of exhibits**, often described as numbering **over 400–500 pieces**.

The museum covers a broad range of categories:

- AvtoVAZ and Lada cars
- Soviet and Russian passenger cars
- Trucks and buses
- Armored vehicles and tanks
- Artillery and missile systems
- Aircraft and helicopters
- Railway equipment
- Naval equipment
- Agricultural machinery
- Construction and industrial machines
- Space and communications-related technology
- Firefighting and emergency vehicles
- Experimental and prototype vehicles

## Connection to AvtoVAZ and Lada

Because the museum was founded by AvtoVAZ, one of its important themes is the history of the Volga Automobile Plant and the Lada brand.

The automotive section has included examples of:

- Early **VAZ / Lada** production cars
- Classic **Zhiguli** models
- Lada Niva vehicles
- Samara-family cars
- Later AvtoVAZ models
- Prototypes, experimental cars, and concept vehicles
- Racing or specialized AvtoVAZ vehicles
- Factory service vehicles and industrial equipment related to car production

The museum helps tell the story of AvtoVAZ’s role in Soviet and Russian mass motorization. The original VAZ-2101, based on the Fiat 124 and sold abroad as a Lada, is especially significant to the company’s history.

## Major exhibit: Submarine B-307

The most famous exhibit is the **diesel-electric submarine B-307**.

### B-307 details

- **Type:** Soviet diesel-electric submarine
- **Project:** Project 641B “Som”, NATO reporting name **Tango-class**
- **Service:** Soviet/Russian Navy
- **Length:** Around 90 meters
- **Status:** Preserved as a museum exhibit
- **Significance:** One of the largest and most unusual museum objects in Tolyatti

The submarine is a major symbol of the museum. It was transported inland and placed on the museum grounds, which was a major logistical undertaking. Its presence makes the museum stand out among Russian technical museums, because full-size submarines are rarely displayed so far from the sea.

Depending on current access arrangements, visitors may be able to view the submarine externally and, at times, tour parts of the interior.

## Military vehicles and weapons

A large part of the collection is devoted to Soviet and Russian military technology.

Typical exhibits have included:

- Tanks
- Self-propelled guns
- Armored personnel carriers
- Infantry fighting vehicles
- Artillery pieces
- Anti-aircraft systems
- Radar and communications equipment
- Missile launchers
- Engineering vehicles
- Military trucks

Examples often associated with this kind of collection include vehicles from the Second World War, Cold War, and postwar Soviet periods, such as:

- **T-34** tanks or related wartime armor
- Heavy tanks and self-propelled guns
- **BMP** and **BTR** armored vehicles
- Soviet artillery systems
- Air defense missile equipment
- Tactical missile launch vehicles

The museum functions partly as a memorial to Soviet engineering and military history.

## Aviation collection

The aviation section includes aircraft and helicopters, usually displayed outdoors.

Exhibits have included various types of:

- Jet fighters
- Trainer aircraft
- Transport aircraft
- Helicopters
- Aircraft engines or aviation equipment

The aircraft are mainly Soviet-designed machines, reflecting the breadth of Soviet aviation technology during the Cold War and late Soviet period.

## Railway exhibits

The museum has also displayed railway equipment, such as:

- Locomotives
- Railway cars
- Industrial rail equipment
- Track-maintenance machines

These exhibits show the role of rail transport in Russian industrial development.

## Civilian vehicles

Beyond AvtoVAZ cars, the museum has included a wide range of Soviet and Russian civilian transport:

- GAZ cars and trucks
- ZIL trucks and limousines
- UAZ off-road vehicles
- Buses
- Fire engines
- Ambulances
- Police and emergency vehicles
- Motorcycles
- Utility vehicles

These exhibits help show everyday Soviet and Russian transport history, not just military or factory history.

## Agricultural and industrial machinery

The museum also preserves machines used in Soviet agriculture and industry, such as:

- Tractors
- Harvesters
- Bulldozers
- Cranes
- Excavators
- Road-building machines
- Factory and municipal equipment

This reflects the museum’s broader mission: preserving the history of technology as a whole, not only automobiles.

## Space and missile-related exhibits

Some displays are connected with Soviet rocketry, air defense, or space-era technology. These may include:

- Missile systems
- Launch-related equipment
- Radar vehicles
- Aerospace components
- Communications equipment

Russia and the Soviet Union had a vast military-industrial and space-industrial complex, so these exhibits fit into the museum’s larger technological narrative.

## Museum layout and visitor experience

The museum is largely arranged as a large outdoor park. Visitors walk between rows or zones of vehicles and machinery. Because many exhibits are exposed to the weather, their condition can vary, but the scale and diversity of the collection make it impressive.

A typical visitor experience includes:

- Walking among tanks, aircraft, locomotives, trucks, and cars
- Seeing AvtoVAZ and Lada models
- Viewing the B-307 submarine
- Learning about Soviet industrial and military engineering
- Taking photographs with large vehicles and aircraft
- Visiting indoor or semi-indoor displays if available

The museum is popular with:

- Car enthusiasts
- Military history fans
- Families
- School groups
- Tourists visiting Tolyatti
- People interested in Soviet technology

## Importance to Tolyatti

Tolyatti is known primarily as an automotive city. AvtoVAZ was one of the USSR’s largest industrial projects, and the city’s modern identity is tied to the factory.

The museum therefore serves several local roles:

1. **Industrial memory** — preserving the history of AvtoVAZ and Soviet engineering.
2. **Educational site** — introducing children and students to machines and technology.
3. **Tourist attraction** — one of the more distinctive places to visit in Tolyatti.
4. **Civic landmark** — representing the city’s identity as a center of heavy industry and automotive production.

## Relationship with AvtoVAZ over time

The museum began as an AvtoVAZ initiative, but over time its organizational status and branding evolved. It became known less simply as the “AvtoVAZ Technical Museum” and more as the **Technical Museum named after K. G. Sakharov** or the **Park Complex of the History of Technology**.

This reflects its expansion beyond being only a factory museum. While AvtoVAZ remains central to its origin and identity, the collection is much broader than Lada cars.

## Notable features

The museum is notable for:

- Its huge open-air scale
- Its association with AvtoVAZ
- Its broad Soviet/Russian technology collection
- Its full-size submarine
- Its combination of cars, tanks, planes, trains, and industrial equipment
- Its importance as one of the main technical museums in the Volga region

## Why it matters

The AvtoVAZ Technical Museum is significant because it preserves physical examples of Soviet and Russian engineering across many fields. Many of the exhibits represent technologies that shaped daily life, industry, war, transport, agriculture, and national infrastructure.

It is not only a car museum, even though AvtoVAZ is central to its story. It is more accurately a **museum of Soviet and Russian technological civilization**, with Lada and AvtoVAZ forming one important part of a much larger picture.

## Practical note

If you plan to visit, check current information before going, because:

- Opening hours may change seasonally
- Some exhibits may be temporarily inaccessible
- Interior access to large exhibits like the submarine may vary
- The museum’s official name and administrative status have changed over time
- Weather matters because much of the collection is outdoors
